title: Microplate Assay for Quantification of Soluble Protein in Ground Coral Samples
author: Rowan McLachlan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdc8i2zw
materials: Equipment needed for making BSA protein standards.

steps.title: Grind Coral Fragments
steps.instruction: Grind frozen coral fragments into a homogeneous paste using a chilled mortar and pestle (chilled via liquid nitrogen or -80 °C freezer for ~20 minutes) or within an ice-bath, ensuring the finest consistency possible for skeletal grains.

steps.title: Weigh and Partition Samples
steps.instruction: Partition the ground coral paste into subsamples for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Tare a pre-baked aluminum weighing pan on a balance.
Transfer all ground coral material from the mortar into the pan and record the total wet weight (grams).
Measure ~0.5 g of wet paste into a pre-labeled 15 ml polypropylene centrifuge tube and record the exact weight of the subsample.
Store the 15 ml tube in a -80 °C freezer immediately.
Transfer remaining material in the pan to a 50 ml centrifuge tube and archive at -80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 1X RIPA Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Dilute concentrated 10X Radioimmunoprecipitation (RIPA) lysis buffer to a 1X solution.

substeps.instruction: Add 15 ml of 10X buffer into a 200 ml Nalgene bottle using a glass graduated cylinder.
Add 135 ml of ultrapure water to the bottle.
Gently swirl until thoroughly mixed.

steps.title: Perform Detergent Lysis
steps.instruction: Extract protein from the coral subsamples using RIPA buffer.

substeps.instruction: Remove ~0.5 g samples from -80 °C freezer and partially defrost at room temperature for 2–5 mins.
Add 1000 µL of 1X RIPA buffer to each tube using a 100-1000 μl pipette with a clean tip per sample.
Scrape inner walls with a clean metal spatula to ensure all particulate matter is submerged.
Keep samples cool in a bucket of crushed ice.
Vigorously vortex each sample for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Perform Freeze-Thaw Lysis
steps.instruction: Complete three cycles of freeze-thaw lysis to ensure full cell disruption.

substeps.instruction: Cycle 1: Partially submerge tubes in liquid nitrogen (max depth 5 cm) for ~10 seconds until frozen; transfer to room temperature water bath for ~2 minutes until defrosted; vortex for 30 seconds.
Cycle 2: Repeat the liquid nitrogen freeze (~10 seconds), water bath defrost (~2 minutes), and vortex (30 seconds).
Cycle 3: Return samples to -80 °C freezer. Alternatively, if proceeding immediately, perform one more liquid nitrogen freeze and water bath defrost.

steps.title: Prepare Centrifuge
steps.instruction: Set up the swing-bucket centrifuge at 4 °C (allow ~10 mins for the condenser to reach temperature).

steps.title: Defrost and Centrifuge Samples
steps.instruction: Isolate the soluble protein from the coral debris.

substeps.instruction: Defrost samples from -80 °C in a room-temperature water bath for ~3 minutes.
Dry the outside of tubes with paper towels or Kim-wipes and vortex for ~30 seconds.
Centrifuge for 20 mins at 4200 rpm / 4122 x g at 4 °C in a balanced configuration.
Gently remove tubes to avoid re-suspending particulates and place upright in crushed ice.

steps.title: Separate Supernatant
steps.instruction: Collect the protein-containing middle phase of the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Using a plastic transfer pipette, transfer only the middle phase of the supernatant to a pre-labeled 2 ml Eppendorf tube, avoiding the upper whitish matrix and lower particulate matter.
Store 2 ml Eppendorfs upright in crushed ice.
Return 15 ml centrifuge tubes (containing matrix and particulates) to the -80 °C freezer for AFDW quantification.

steps.title: Prepare BSA Standards
steps.instruction: Prepare a series of BSA standards (0 to 500 μg/ml) on the day of the assay using ultrapure water as the diluent.

substeps.instruction: Label eight 5 ml conical Eppendorf tubes (A-H).
Dilute a 1 ml ampule of BSA stock according to Table 1.
Mix by tipping and swirling (do not shake); if bubbles form, centrifuge for 1 min at 4000 rpm.

steps.title: Prepare Dye Reagent
steps.instruction: Prepare 150 ml of 1X Bio-Rad protein assay dye reagent.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 30 ml of concentrated dye and 120 ml of ultrapure water into a clean Erlenmeyer flask.
Gently swirl to mix and cover with Parafilm.

steps.title: Load and Dilute Samples in Microplates
steps.instruction: Prepare samples in a 96-well microplate format using Plate A for dilution and Plate B for the assay.

substeps.instruction: Label two 96-well plates as 'A' and 'B'.
Dispense 5 µl of supernatant from each 2 ml Eppendorf into columns 2–10 of Plate A in triplicate (using a 20 μl pipette).
Return 2 ml Eppendorf tubes to -80 °C freezer.
Add 20 µl of ultrapure water to the sample wells in Plate A using a multichannel pipette (1:5 dilution).
Mix on a 96-well plate shaker for 1 minute.
Transfer 10 µl from each diluted sample well in Plate A to the corresponding well in Plate B using a multichannel pipette.

steps.title: Load Standards and Dye
steps.instruction: Complete the Bradford assay setup in Plate B.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 10 µl of each BSA standard (A-H) into column 1 of Plate B (Standard A in 1A, etc.).
Add 190 µl of 1X diluted dye reagent to every well in Plate B using a 200 μl multichannel pipette.
Record the time of dye addition.
Mix on a shake-plate for 1 minute.
Incubate at room temperature for at least 5 minutes (maximum 1 hour).
Pop any air bubbles in the wells using a clean pipette tip.

steps.title: Measure Absorbance
steps.instruction: Quantify protein concentration using a microplate reader.

substeps.instruction: Measure absorbance at 595 nm using a FlexStation® 3 reader with SoftMax Pro software.
Use the software to average triplicates, correct for blanks (G1 and H1), and calculate the Adjusted mean concentration (mg/ml) via the calibration curve.

steps.title: Calculate Protein Energy Content
steps.instruction: Determine the total protein energy and AFDW of the subsample.

substeps.instruction: Calculate Final volume of subsample (ml) = Volume of ground coral subsample (ml) + Volume of RIPA buffer added (ml), assuming 1 g paste = 1 ml.
Calculate Weight of protein in subsample (mg) = Adjusted mean concentration (mg/ml) x Final volume of subsample (ml).
Calculate Energy content of protein in subsample (J) = Weight of protein (mg) x 23.9 J mg-1.

steps.title: Determine Ash-Free Dry Weight (AFDW)
steps.instruction: Quantify the organic matter of the subsample to normalize protein data.

substeps.instruction: Combine the remaining 15ml tube contents and the 2 ml Eppendorf (soluble protein) into pre-baked, pre-labeled aluminum pans.
Prepare a control by dispensing 1000 µl of 1X RIPA into a separate pre-labeled aluminum pan.
Dry all pans in a 60 °C oven overnight; cool for 5–10 minutes and weigh in triplicate to get 'Dried Pan Weights'.
Burn pans in a muffle furnace at 450 ºC for 5 hours; cool for 5–10 minutes and weigh in triplicate to get 'Burnt Pan Weights'.
Calculate AFDW of the subsample (g) using Equation 4: [avg CORAL Dried - avg CORAL Burnt] / [avg CONTROL Dried - avg CONTROL Burnt].
Calculate total protein energy (J g-1) = Energy content of protein (J) ÷ AFDW of subsample (g).

If required, calculate surface area (SA) of subsample (cm2) = [wet weight subsample (g) ÷ total wet weight fragment (g)] x SA whole colony (cm2), and calculate total protein energy (J cm-2) = Energy content (J) ÷ SA subsample (cm2).
